reReview2.scope: PR #21 fix commit c7144bb (round 3 — bounded cap)
distinctDefectsFixed: P2 safeUrl over-strip + navigation-mask: a no-path URL with '@' in the query (e.g. https://shop.example.com?contact=bob@mail.net) had its authority scan include the query, so lastIndexOf('@') replaced the host with the post-'@' text — wrong host echoed AND a navigation mismatch could be masked (both sides normalizing to the same junk).
P2 safeUrl bypass: a leading space (or any char before the scheme) made the ^-anchored scheme regex miss, skipping userinfo stripping entirely -> credential leaked.
P3 safeUrl leak: a '/' inside the userinfo truncated the authority scan before the '@', leaving the credential unstripped.
reReview2.resolution: ARCHITECTURE CHANGE (beyond the 3-round cap, deliberately): replaced the hand-rolled string parser with the WHATWG URL parser (render host+path only; a scheme'd URL the parser rejects is REDACTED to its scheme, never echoed; a relative URL echoes its clean path). This eliminates the entire hand-rolled-parser leak class by construction. Justified beyond the cap because a confirmed secret-leak into evidence violates a NON-NEGOTIABLE hard rule ('No secrets in evidence'), which overrides the review-loop-count convention — same precedent as PR #6 (concurrency class eliminated by switching to the correct mechanism rather than patching).
reReview2.regressionTests: 1 new round-3 test (no-path @-in-query keeps real host + no mask; leading-whitespace stripped; /-in-userinfo redacted; navigation does not falsely match two hosts sharing a post-@ tail). 18 in-package, 449/449 repo-wide.

reReview3.scope: PR #21 fix commit 2d4badd (round 4 — focused safeUrl verification)
distinctDefectsFixed: P1 (round-3 WHATWG rewrite still leaked): for an OPAQUE-path scheme (foo:user:pass@host/path, custom:...) the parser leaves userinfo INSIDE pathname (host empty, origin null), so origin+pathname re-emitted 'user:pass@'.

P1: a blob: URL carrying an authenticated inner URL (blob:https://user:pass@host/uuid) has origin derived from the inner URL (not null) and pathname = the whole inner URL text, so origin+pathname concatenated and leaked the inner userinfo.
P3: blob:/data:/about: were mangled (origin duplicated; ':' -> '://').
reReview3.resolution: Final invariant: render `protocol//host/pathname` ONLY when url.host is non-empty (a true authority — the parser then isolates userinfo into username/password and never into host/pathname); REDACT every opaque-path or parser-rejected scheme to its scheme. Provably complete: userinfo is parser-isolable ONLY with an authority, so host!=='' is exactly the safe-to-render set; query/fragment are never included (we use host+pathname, never search/hash).
reReview3.regressionTests: 1 new round-4 test (foo:/custom:/blob: opaque schemes with embedded userinfo are redacted, never re-emitted). 19 in-package, 450/450 repo-wide.

reReview4.scope: PR #21 fix commit e498a47 (round 5 — final safeUrl confirmation)
distinctDefectsFixed: P1: the catch branch redacted only when hasScheme was true, so a scheme-less protocol-relative URL ('//user:SECRET@host:999999/path') whose malformed authority made new URL throw fell through to the naive split and echoed the userinfo. The catch now redacts any authority-bearing input (hasScheme || raw.startsWith('//')); only a bare relative path (no authority => no userinfo) is echoed.
reReview4.regressionTests: 1 new round-5 test (malformed protocol-relative //user:SECRET@... redacted; well-formed //user:pw@host/app.js shows host+path, userinfo stripped). 20 in-package, 451/451 repo-wide.

reReview5.scope: PR #21 fix commit 88a6776 (round 6 — final safeUrl confirmation)
distinctDefectsFixed: P1: a backslash-form authority (\\user:SECRET@evil.com:999999/p) — WHATWG normalizes \\ to // for special schemes, parses userinfo, then throws on the bad port — slipped the catch's startsWith('//') prefix check (backslashes, not forward slashes) and was echoed verbatim. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: the catch now REDACTS UNCONDITIONALLY on any parse failure, so no unparsed string is ever echoed. safeUrl is now leak-proof by construction: it returns ONLY parser-rendered protocol//host/pathname (host non-empty => userinfo isolated by the parser, query/fragment excluded), a clean relative pathname (no authority => no userinfo), or a redaction marker.
reReview5.regressionTests: 1 new round-6 test (backslash / slash-backslash malformed authority redacted, no userinfo echoed). 21 in-package, 452/452 repo-wide.
reReview5.leakVectorCountByRound: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 -> 0 (catch no longer enumerates prefixes; always redacts on parse failure)
